analyses.what_happens: Reset is released at step 1. Step 4: i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=1, so a request is accepted: i_a_opcode=1 (PutPartialData), i_a_address=0x000 (ALERT_TEST), i_a_size=2, i_a_mask=1111, i_a_data=0x80000001, i_a_intg_flip=0, i_a_source=0. Its D beat is at step 5 (o_d_valid=1, i_d_ready=1, o_d_error=0, o_d_source=0). Steps 6 and 8 accept writes to CTRL (0x004) with intg_flip=0. The intg_flip=1 values at steps 3 and 7 come with i_a_valid=0, so they are never accepted and flip_seen stays 0. At step 9 o_alert=1, which is 4 edges after the D beat. The checker counts no qualifying write: q_cnt=0, a_cnt=0, age=31, and p_qual is 0 because the step-4 write was not PutFullData. Both parts (a) and (b) of a_CHK_003 fail at step 9.
analyses.spec_says: rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:625-627 (INT-ALERT-003, RT-5-06): "A write of 1 to `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` triggers one alert event, as the register description says." rules.json RT-T5.2.1-03: "Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind." rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:667 (D-009): "Tests that trigger an alert write 0x8000_0001 (regwen kept at 1) ... One write of 1 to `fatal_fault` ... gives exactly one `o_alert` pulse, no later than 16 cycles after the write response." None of these limits the opcode. rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:671 (D-013): "Checked cases: full-word writes with mask 1111 succeed". contract.json:769 (CHK-029): "Full-word writes with mask 1111 succeed for both PutFullData and PutPartialData." TL spec rule TL-T3.1.3.4-05 defines PutPartialData with a_size=2 as a 4-byte write. The step-4 request is therefore a legal write of 1 to fatal_fault with regwen=1, and one alert within 16 cycles of its D beat is the required behaviour. However, contract.json:302 (the CHK-003 behaviour text) defines a 'Qualifying write' only as "a PutFullData with a_size=2 and mask 1111 to 0x000". The contract text is narrower than the spec.
analyses.rtl_does: tlul_adapter_reg.sv:155 `assign wr_req = a_ack & ((tl_i.a_opcode == PutFullData) | (tl_i.a_opcode == PutPartialData));` and :158 `assign we_o = wr_req & ~err_internal;` handle both opcodes the same way. rv_timer_reg_top.sv:615 `assign alert_test_we = racl_addr_hit_write[0] & reg_we & !reg_error;` and :175 `assign alert_test_gated_we = alert_test_we && alert_test_regwen_qs;` do not depend on the opcode. rv_timer.sv:148-150 drives alert_test from `reg2hw.alert_test.q & reg2hw.alert_test.qe` into the alert sender, so a full-word PutPartialData of 0x80000001 produces one alert handshake. That is the o_alert pulse at step 9, 4 cycles after the D beat. This matches the spec.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_alert.sv:55-56 `assign wr0_w = acc_w && (i_a_opcode == 3'd0) && (i_a_size == 2'd2) && (i_a_mask == 4'hF) && (i_a_address == 32'h0);` accepts only opcode 0. So qual_w (line 57), p_qual (line 86), q_cnt (line 89) and age (line 78) never count a full-word PutPartialData write to ALERT_TEST. The assertion at lines 105-108 needs `q_cnt + qual_w - qerr >= a_cnt+1` and `(p_valid && p_qual) || qual_w || age <= 16`, and both are false at step 9. The regwen model has the same gap: p_clr at line 87 uses wr0_w, so a PutPartialData full-word write with bit 31=0 would clear regwen in the DUT but not in the model. The checker does follow the contract text at contract.json:302.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec makes alert triggering depend only on writing 1 to fatal_fault (RT-5-06 at spec:627, D-009 at spec:667). It says full-word mask-1111 writes succeed (D-013 at spec:671), and CHK-029 (contract.json:769) states this explicitly for both PutFullData and PutPartialData. The checker's wr0_w (nnc_chk_alert.sv:55) restricts qualifying writes to opcode 0, so the DUT's correct alert at step 9 is flagged as spurious. The same restriction affects p_clr (line 87), so the regwen model is wrong for PutPartialData as well.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker follows the CHK-003 contract text exactly (contract.json:302: "a PutFullData with a_size=2 and mask 1111"). The defect is in the contract derivation as well as in the SVA.

candidates.evidence_for: The CHK-003 contract text and the CHK-014 stimulus (contract.json:487) use only PutFullData. A reader could take PutFullData as the intended alert-test opcode.
candidates.evidence_against: The specification does not restrict the opcode anywhere. D-013 and CHK-029 say both opcodes succeed for mask 1111, and INT-TL-003 (spec:592-595) treats all TL-UL requests as legal stimulus. The ambiguity is in the contract, not in the spec.

candidates.evidence_for: No environment obligation would exclude this sequence. The checked trace keeps i_a_valid=0 at the first edge after release (step 1), has no accepted intg_flip request, uses distinct sources and param=0, and ENV-07 (nnc_env.sv:100-102) is met because data[31]=1.
candidates.evidence_against: No spec rule forbids PutPartialData writes to ALERT_TEST, so adding an assumption against them would hide real behaviour and is not supported.

candidates.evidence_for: None found. The alert fires once, 4 cycles after the D beat of a write of 1 to fatal_fault.
candidates.evidence_against: rv_timer_reg_top.sv:615/175 and tlul_adapter_reg.sv:155 implement exactly the specified opcode-independent behaviour.

analyses.options: 1) Fix the checker and the contract text: in nnc_chk_alert.sv:55 change `(i_a_opcode == 3'd0)` to `((i_a_opcode == 3'd0) || (i_a_opcode == 3'd1))`. That covers qual_w and p_clr/regwen, which both derive from wr0_w. Update the CHK-003 behaviour text in contract.json:302 to say "a PutFullData or PutPartialData with a_size=2 and mask 1111" for both the regwen model and the qualifying write. 2) If the designer decides that only PutFullData counts as an alert-test write, record that as a new decision in spec section 8 first, then add a matching assumption in nnc_env.sv. Without that spec decision, this option is not supported. Do not weaken the 16-cycle bound or the count bound.

analyses.what_happens: Reset is released at step 1, and the request accepted at step 1 is a byte write to INTR_ENABLE0: i_a_opcode=0 (PutFullData), i_a_address=0x100, i_a_size=0, i_a_mask=0001, i_a_data=0x40000001 (bit 0=1), intg_flip=0. Its D beat is at step 2 with o_d_error=0. The checker records q_w100=1 but a_upd=0, so at the pop the model ie stays 0 while the DUT's IE_0 becomes 1. Step 3 accepts a PutFullData byte write (size 0, mask 0001) of data bit 0=1 to 0x108 (INTR_TEST0), which sets IS_0. At step 5 rst_ni=1, model ie=0, c100=0, and dw0/dw1/dw2=0 because the 0x100 D beat was at step 2. o_intr_timer_expired=1, so a_CHK_004 fails. The trace also has i_a_valid=1 at step 1, the first edge after rst_ni rises. D-016 forbids that, but it does not cause the failure.
analyses.spec_says: rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:671 (D-013): "a byte write (a_size 0, mask 0001, offset aligned) to byte 0 of CTRL, INTR_ENABLE0, INTR_STATE0 or INTR_TEST0 completes with `d_error` = 0 and has the effect of the write." No opcode is restricted. TL rule TL-T3.1.3.4-04 (PutFullData): "a_size should be 'h2 ... though the bus specification allows these to be defined otherwise". spec:663 (D-005, RT-8-07): "`o_intr_timer_expired` shall equal `IS_0` AND `IE_0` except in the 2 cycles after either changes." rules.json CP-T1.8.6-04: interrupt = INTR_STATE masked (ANDed) with INTR_ENABLE. contract.json:316 (CHK-004 text) updates ie only for "a PutFullData/PutPartialData with a_size=2 and mask 1111 or a PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 0001". This leaves out the PutFullData byte write that D-013 covers. Separately, spec:674 (D-016, RT-8-29): "The test bench keeps `i_a_valid` = 0 while `rst_ni` = 0 and in the first cycle after release."
analyses.rtl_does: tlul_err.sv:58-80: for a_size=0, mask_chk/fulldata_chk pass for mask 0001 at address[1:0]=0, so a PutFullData byte write is legal. tlul_adapter_reg.sv:155 issues it as a write. rv_timer_reg_top.sv:623 `assign intr_enable0_we = racl_addr_hit_write[2] & reg_we & !reg_error;` and wr_err at lines 601-611 only reject byte enables outside the register's permit (INTR_ENABLE0 is 1 bit wide), so IE_0 <= 1. INTR_TEST0 (line 629) sets IS_0 the same way. prim_intr_hw.sv:100/109 drives `intr_o = state & enable`, giving o_intr_timer_expired=1 at step 5. This is correct: IE_0=1 and IS_0=1.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_intr.sv:62-64 `wire a_upd = n_flip && (i_a_address == 32'h100) && ((is_wr && i_a_size == 2'd2 && i_a_mask == 4'b1111) || (i_a_opcode == 3'd1 && i_a_size == 2'd0 && i_a_mask == 4'b0001));` updates ie for a byte write only when the opcode is PutPartialData. Line 98 `if (q_upd[rp] && !o_d_error) ie <= q_d0[rp];` therefore leaves ie=0 after the PutFullData byte write. The assertion at lines 107-108 then requires o_intr_timer_expired=0 once c100==0 and dw0..dw2 are clear. The checker follows contract.json:316 to the letter.

candidates.evidence_for: D-013 (spec:671) says any aligned byte write with a_size 0 and mask 0001 to INTR_ENABLE0 "has the effect of the write", with no opcode restriction. The DUT applies it (rv_timer_reg_top.sv:623), but the checker's IE model (nnc_chk_intr.sv:62-64) ignores the PutFullData variant. The checker then expects 0 while IS_0 AND IE_0 = 1, which RT-8-07/CP-T1.8.6-04 require to be 1.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker follows the contract text (contract.json:316), so the contract needs fixing as well.

candidates.evidence_for: The request at step 1 is presented at the first edge after rst_ni rises (step 0 rst_ni=0, step 1 rst_ni=1, i_a_valid=1). This breaks D-016/RT-8-29 (spec:674). nnc_env.sv:66 only assumes `if (!rst_ni) assume (!i_a_valid);` and does not cover the first cycle after release (see CHK-008).
candidates.evidence_against: The violation is incidental. If the same PutFullData byte write were accepted one cycle later, the DUT would behave the same and the checker's IE model would still miss the update. Adding the missing assumption would only shift the counterexample, not remove it.

candidates.evidence_for: TL-T3.1.3.4-04 says PutFullData "should" use a_size 2. The contract and the CHK-018 stimulus (contract.json:560) only use PutPartialData for byte writes, so the authors may have treated a PutFullData byte write as out of scope.
candidates.evidence_against: D-013 is opcode-neutral, and INT-TL-003 (spec:592-595) makes every TL-UL request legal stimulus. The TL spec explicitly allows other sizes for PutFullData.

candidates.evidence_for: None. The interrupt rises only after IE_0 was written to 1 and IS_0 was set via INTR_TEST0.
candidates.evidence_against: prim_intr_hw.sv:100/109 implements state AND enable, and the byte write is handled as D-013 requires.

analyses.options: 1) Fix the checker and the contract: in nnc_chk_intr.sv:64 change `(i_a_opcode == 3'd1 && i_a_size == 2'd0 && i_a_mask == 4'b0001)` to `(is_wr && i_a_size == 2'd0 && i_a_mask == 4'b0001)`. Change the CHK-004 text at contract.json:316 to "a PutFullData/PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 0001". Do the same review for other byte-write models, such as CHK-011's error=0 list, which only names PutPartialData. 2) Independently, add the D-016 first-cycle-after-release assumption to nnc_env.sv (see CHK-008), so later counterexamples do not use an illegal step-1 request. 3) If the designer wants byte writes to INTR_ENABLE0 to use PutPartialData only, a spec decision must say so before an environment assumption is added. No such rule exists today.

analyses.what_happens: Step 0: rst_ni=0 and i_a_valid=0. Step 1: rst_ni rises, and at that same first edge after release i_a_valid=1 with o_a_ready=1. The request is a PutFullData to 0x000, a_size=0, mask 1000, data 0x40000000, source 128. In the checker, rst_q is still 0 at step 1, so the term `(rst_ni && !rst_q) ? !i_a_valid : 1'b1` is false and a_CHK_008 fails at step 1. No other part of the obligation is violated: param=0, address<0x200, mask 1000 is not on the bad list, instr=0, the source is free, and the data is not 0x00000001.
analyses.spec_says: rv_timer_Design_Specification.md:674 (D-016, rules.json RT-8-29): "The test bench keeps `i_a_valid` = 0 while `rst_ni` = 0 and in the first cycle after release." contract.json:376 (CHK-008 (2)): "i_a_valid=0 at every edge with rst_ni=0 and at the first edge after rst_ni rises." This is an obligation on the environment (the test bench).
analyses.rtl_does: Not involved: CHK-008 only checks inputs. The DUT accepts the request (o_a_ready=1), but the property does not look at DUT behaviour.
analyses.checker_does: nnc_chk_tbhost.sv:57 `rst_q <= rst_ni;` holds the previous reset value. Line 86 `((rst_ni && !rst_q) ? !i_a_valid : 1'b1)` encodes D-016's first-cycle-after-release rule and matches the spec. The environment, however, only assumes nnc_env.sv:66 `always @(*) if (!rst_ni) assume (!i_a_valid);` (ENV-01, which cites RT-8-29). Nothing constrains i_a_valid at the first edge with rst_ni=1 after reset, so the solver is free to violate the stimulus self-check.

candidates.evidence_for: D-016/RT-8-29 (spec:674) puts an obligation on the test bench: i_a_valid=0 "in the first cycle after release". ENV-01 (nnc_env.sv:65-66) only implements the 'while rst_ni = 0' half. The counterexample breaks exactly the missing half, at step 1, and nothing else.
candidates.evidence_against: None. The checker term at nnc_chk_tbhost.sv:86 matches the rule word for word.

candidates.evidence_for: rst_q has no reset or initial value (nnc_chk_tbhost.sv:34/57), so in formal its value at step 0 is solver-chosen. That only matters at step 0, where rst_ni=0 already forces the check anyway.
candidates.evidence_against: The failure is at step 1 with rst_q=0 correctly following rst_ni=0 at step 0. The checker logic matches the contract text (contract.json:376) and D-016.
The property only constrains inputs, so DUT behaviour cannot cause this failure.

analyses.options: 1) Add the missing half of D-016/RT-8-29 to nnc_env.sv, for example: `reg f_rst_q = 1'b0; always @(posedge clk_i) f_rst_q <= rst_ni; always @(*) if (rst_ni && !f_rst_q) assume (!i_a_valid);`. Then re-run CHK-008 and the other checks; CHK-004's current trace also uses an illegal step-1 request. 2) Also consider whether the other CHK-008 obligations not yet assumed should be added to nnc_env.sv, since each is a spec-backed environment rule: (3) bad masks 0101/1001/1010/1011/1101 per TL-T3.1.3.4-02; (3) the exact-data rule against writing 0x00000001 to word 0 for all masks and sizes per RT-8-15; (4) the pending-CTRL-write condition and byte-write CTRL tracking per RT-8-03. Otherwise the formal run of CHK-008 will keep producing environment-only counterexamples. Do not weaken the checker term at nnc_chk_tbhost.sv:86.
